distanthorizons.config.title: Far Skylines settings
distanthorizons.config.client.quickEnabl: If true, Far Skylines will draw LODs outside the vanilla draw breadth.
distanthorizons.config.client.quickShowW: If true then the world making / intaking inroads will be shown on the screen when running.
distanthorizons.config.client.qualityPre:
Switches a bunch of sightly settings to quickly switch Far Skylines' drawing loveliness. 

Lower this setting if your GPU is overloaded or you are having framespeed snags.
distanthorizons.config.client.threadPres:
Switches how many threads Far Skylines will brook. 

Upping this setting will up the Far Maker's speed and LOD loading speed, 
but will also up CPU/RAM brooking and may bring in stuttering.

Heed: This is a CPU beholden setting. 
It should put an even deal of strain on a 2 core CPU as a 64 core CPU.

distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.g:
Distant Horizons' render distance, measured in chunks. 

Note: this be a best effort number. 
Th' actual render distance may be above or below this number 
depending on yer other graphic settings.

This shows how far apart th' drops in LOD quality be. 

Higher settings will increase th' distance between drops 
but will increase memory and GPU usage.

Th' maximum detail LODs can render at. 

§6Fastest:§r Chunk
§6Fanciest:§r Block

How well LODs show overhangs, caves, cliff-sides, an' all. 

Higher options will increase memory and GPU usage.
Use Camera Pos fer Quality Drop-Off

If true DH will try ter use th' camera position when 
settin' th' LOD quality drop-off. 
If false DH will use th' player's position. 

Enablin' helps free-cam mods render proper. 
Disablin' helps multi-camera mods render proper (ie Immersive Portals or camera mods).

If true LOD quality will increase when th' camera be zoomed in, 
like when usin' a spyglass or zoom mod. 

Only LODs visible through th' camera view be affected. 

When zoomed in LODs will load ter th' same detail level 
they would have if ye were close ter them.

How many detail levels zoomin' in can increase LOD quality by. 
Higher numbers allow stronger zooms ter render crisper terrain, 
but will increase memory and GPU usage while zoomed in. 

A vanilla spyglass needs 4 detail levels ter reach its full quality.

How quick LODs drop off in quality. 

Larger numbers will improve how distant terrain looks 
but will increase memory and GPU usage.

Sets how LODs should be shaded. 
Can be used ter improve shader compatibility.
How should th' sides an' bottom o' grass block LODs render?

If true nearby LODs will render blocks with their real shape 
instead of full cubes. 
If false all LODs render as full cubes. 

Only applies to the highest detail LODs.

If true LODs will fade away as ye get closer ter them. 
If false LODs will cut off sudden-like at a set distance from th' camera. 
This settin' be affected by th' vanilla overdraw prevention config.

How should vanilla Minecraft fade inter Distant Horizons LODs? 

NONE: Fastest, thar will be a might-y border between DH an' MC renderin'. 
SINGLE_PASS: Fades after MC's transparent pass, opaque blocks underwater won't be faded. 
DOUBLE_PASS: Slowest, fades after both MC's opaque an' transparent passes, gives th' smoothest transition.

Should DH fade out before reachin' th' far clip plane? 
This be helpful ter keep DH clouds from cuttin' off in th' distance.

How bright LOD colors be. 

0 = black 
1 = normal 
2 = near white

How saturated LOD colors be. 

0 = black an' white 
1 = normal 
2 = bright an' bold

This be th' same as th' vanilla Biome Blendin' settin's fer th' LOD area. 

Note: anythin' above '0' will slow down LOD loadin' time. 

'0' be th' same as Vanilla Biome Blendin' o' '1x1', 
'1' be th' same as Vanilla Biome Blendin' o' '3x3', 
'2' be th' same as Vanilla Biome Blendin' o' '5x5'...
Ambient Occlusion adds depth ter th' lightin' o' blocks.
Enablin' Anti-Aliasing smooths edges an' cuts th' flickerin' when movin'.

If true th' non-terrain objects will be rendered by DH. 
like beacon beams an' clouds.
Sets th' maximum height beacons will render up ter. Needs a world re-load ter take effect.

If true LOD beacon beams will be rendered wider at extreme distances, 
makin' them easier ter see. 
If false all LOD beacon beams will only ever be 1 block wide.
If true LOD beacon beams will be rendered.
If true LOD clouds will be rendered.

A comma separated list o' dimension resource locations where DH clouds will render. 

Example: "minecraft:overworld,minecraft:the_end" 

Changes need a world re-load.

False = DH will render a single layer o' clouds, like vanilla Minecraft. 
True = DH will render 3 layers o' clouds at different heights.
Sets if fog be drawn on DH LODs.
Th' color o' th' fog on LODs.

§6True:§r Minecraft renders fog like normal. 
§6False:§r disables Minecraft's fog on vanilla chunks. 

May cause issues with other mods that edit fog.

Where should th' fog start? 

  '0.0': Fog starts at th' player's position. 
  '1.0': Th' fog-start's circle fits just in th' lod render distance square. 
'1.414': Th' lod render distance square fits just in th' fog-start's circle.

Where should th' fog end? 

  '0.0': Fog ends at th' player's position. 
  '1.0': Th' fog-end's circle fits just in th' lod render distance square. 
'1.414': Th' lod render distance square fits just in th' fog-end's circle.

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': No fog at all. 
  '1.0': Full fog color.

What be th' maximum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': No fog at all. 
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How should th' fog thickness be calculated? 

LINEAR: Linear based on distance (will ignore 'density') 
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(distance*density)) 
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((distance*density)^2))

Sets how height affects fog. 
When in doubt start with SPHERICAL, ADDITION, or MAX. 

SPHERICAL: Fog is calculated based on camera distance. 
CYLINDRICAL: Ignore height, fog is calculated based on horizontal distance. 
MAX: max(heightFog, farFog) 
ADDITION: heightFog + farFog 
MULTIPLY: heightFog * farFog 
INVERSE_MULTIPLY: 1 - (1-heightFog) * (1-farFog) 
LIMITED_ADDITION: farFog + max(farFog, heightFog) 
MULTIPLY_ADDITION: farFog + farFog * heightFog 
INVERSE_MULTIPLY_ADDITION: farFog + 1 - (1-heightFog) * (1-farFog) 
AVERAGE: farFog*0.5 + heightFog*0.5

Where should th' height fog be located? 

ABOVE_CAMERA: Height fog starts from camera ter th' sky 
BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog starts from camera ter th' void 
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog starts from camera ter both th' sky an' th' void 
ABOVE_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height ter th' sky 
BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height ter th' void 
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog starts from a set height ter both th' sky an' th' void
If th' height fog be calculated around a set height, what be that height position?

How far should th' start o' height fog offset? 

  '0.0': Fog starts with no offset. 
  '1.0': Fog starts with th' offset o' th' entire world's height. (Include depth)

How far should th' end o' height fog offset? 

  '0.0': Fog ends with no offset. 
  '1.0': Fog ends with th' offset o' th' entire world's height. (Include depth)

What be th' minimum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': No fog at all. 
  '1.0': Full fog color.

What be th' maximum fog thickness? 

  '0.0': No fog at all. 
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How should th' height fog thickness be calculated? 

LINEAR: Linear based on height (will ignore 'density') 
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(height*density)) 
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((height*density)^2))
What be th' height fog's density?

If true th' nearby an' zoomed-in LODs will render with their block's 
actual texture and silhouette instead o' a single flat color. 

Only applies ter high detail LODs where th' texture be actually visible, 
distant LODs always use flat colors. 
Has no effect while a shader pack be active, since shader packs 
render LODs with their own programs.

Th' highest detail level number that can render with block textures. 
At higher detail levels each LOD covers multiple blocks, 
makin' textures smaller than a pixel an' so invisible. 

Larger numbers texture more distant LODs 
but increase memory usage.

that DH won't render textures on.

Example: "minecraft:grass_block,nylium"

Block Tags Don't Use Side Texture

that DH will render their sides usin' th' bottom texture. 

Example: "grass_blocks,nylium"

Example: "minecraft:beacon"

Sets how intense th' noise texture be.

Set ter 0 ter stop noise from fadin' away.

Sets how far from th' camera Distant Horizons will start renderin'. 
Measured as a percentage o' th' vanilla render distance. 
-1 = Auto, overdraw will change based on th' vanilla render distance. 

Higher values will stop LODs from renderin' behind vanilla blocks at a higher distance, 
but may cause holes ter appear in th' LODs. 
Holes be most likely ter appear when flyin' through unloaded terrain. 

Increasin' th' vanilla render distance increases th' effectiveness o' this settin'.

If set ter true th' overdraw prevention radius will get closer 
ter th' camera when flyin'/movin' quick. 

This helps reduce issues where Minecraft can't load or 
generate chunks fast enough ter keep up with DH.

with a skylight value o' 0 under th' cave cullin' height in dimensions that 
do not have a ceiling.

If true beacons near th' camera won't be drawn ter stop vanilla overdraw. 
If false all beacons will be rendered.

ain't drawn, increasin' GPU performance.

th' player's camera, decreasin' GPU performance. 

Disable this if ye see LODs disappearin' at th' corners o' yer vision.

Same as th' other frustum cullin' option except that it be

an' th' shadow pass be bein' rendered. 

Disable this if shadows render wrong.

A comma separated list o' block resource locations that won't be rendered by DH. 
Air be always in this list. 

Note: 
If ye see gaps, or holes ye may have ter change 
worldCompression ter [MERGE_SAME_BLOCKS] an' re-generate th' LODs.

A comma separated list o' block resource locations that shouldn't be rendered

Air be always in this list. 

Defaults ter an empty list since most cave blocks will be ignored on their own fer bein': 
transparent, non-solid, or liquids, but new blocks can be added here if needed.

distanthorizons.config.common.worldGener: World Generator
Enable Distant Generation

§6True:§r in single player LODs will be created outside th' vanilla render distance. 
Depending on th' Generator Mode pre-existing chunks will be important an'/o 
missing chunks will be generated. 
Note: this can use a large amount o' CPU. 

§6False:§r LODs will only generate within th' vanilla render distance.
Distant Generator Plan

Sets how LODs will be generated 
outside th' vanilla render distance 
in singleplayer. 

Some options may not be available dependin' on th' MC version. 

§6SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS§r 
Recommended fer modded or vanilla worlds. 

§6SURFACE_ONLY§r 
Recommended fer computers that don't have 
enough CPU power or RAM space ter handle 
chunk generation. 

§6CHUNKS_ONLY§r 
Recommended fer custom worlds 
where th' surface generator would 
generate wrong terrain. 

§6DISABLED§r 
Recommended if ye be havin' lag.
Chunk Generator Mode
How complicated th' generation should be when generatin' LODs outside th' vanilla render distance.
Enable Fast Surface Gen

Needs a world restart ter change. 

If enabled Distant Horizons will very quickly generate a 
rough estimate o' th' terrain surface ter 
fill out th' render distance. 

After th' surface be generated Distant Horizons 
will then generate th' individual chunks as set 
by yer "distantGeneratorMode" config ter get 
trees an' structures. 

It be recommended ter disable this option 
if ye have a completely custom world, 
ter keep yer eyes off normal terrain.
Show Generation Progress
Sets how th' distant generator progress should be shown.
Progress Display Interval In Seconds
Sets how long between progress update displays.
Seconds Ter Show Progress Hiding Instructions

Fer how many seconds should instructions fer disablin' th' distant generator progress be shown? 
Setting this ter 0 hides th' instructional message so th' world gen progress be shown right away when it starts.
Show Generation Speed in Chunks/Second

When loggin' generation progress also include th' rate at which chunks 
be bein' generated. 
This can be useful fer troubleshoot'n performance.
Limit If Server Be Ailin'

If th' Minecraft server thread be takin' too long 
Distant Horizons will pause world gen ter reduce server stutterin'/lag.
Pause If Movin' Quick

If th' player/camera be movin' quick 
Distant Horizons will pause world gen ter improve loadin' speed 
an' reduce lag.
Surface Regen Max Distance Percent

Th' percentage o' th' full LOD render distance 
that th' second pass o' th' fast surface generator will 
fill with chunks generated as set by yer 
"distantGeneratorMode".
distanthorizons.config.common.lodBuildin:
Disablin' this check may fix issues where LODs ain't updated after 
blocks have been changed.

What algorithm should be used ter compress new LOD data? 
This settin' will only affect new or updated LOD data, 
any data already generated when this settin' be changed will be 
unaffected until it needs ter be re-written ter th' database. 

Fastest: LZ4 
Highest Compression: LZMA2

How should block data be compressed when creatin' LOD data? 
This settin' will only affect new or updated LOD data, 
any data already generated when this settin' be changed will be 
unaffected until it be modified or re-loaded. 

Most Accurate: Merge Same Blocks 
Highest Compression: Visually Equal

Needs a level restart ter apply. 

Setting this ter a less strict mode increases DB read/write 
speed at th' cost o' possible data loss/corruption if 
th' computer loses power 
(unexpected program shutdown should be safe fer all options). 

§6FULL§r 
ACID - data will never be lost or corrupted 
Slow 

§6NORMAL§r 
Some data may be lost on power loss, but th' database shouldn't be corrupted. 
Fast 

§6OFF§r 
Th' database may be corrupted during power loss 
Faster
Upsample Lower Detail LODs Ter Fill Holes

When active DH will try ter fill missin' LOD data 
with any data that be present in th' tree, stoppin' holes when movin' 
when a N-sized generator (or server) be active. 

§6EXPERIMENTAL§r Will increase harddrive use an' may cause renderin' issues. 
See th' config file fer more details.
distanthorizons.config.common.multiThrea: How many threads DH will use.

What Java thread priority should DH's primary thread pools run with? 

Ye probably don't need ter change this unless ye be also 
runnin' C2ME an' be seein' thread starvation in either C2ME or DH.

If C2ME be present, set DH's thread count ter match C2ME. 

This be needed ter stop thread starvation issues when C2ME be present.
distanthorizons.config.common.logging.@t: Sets how loggin' should be handled.

distanthorizons.config.server.sendLevelK:
Makes th' server send level keys fer each world. 
Disable this if ye use other ways ter send level keys.
distanthorizons.config.server.levelKeyPr:
Prefix o' th' level keys sent ter th' clients. 
If th' mod be runnin' behind a proxy, each backend should use a unique value. 
If this value be empty, th' level key will be based on th' server's seed hash.
distanthorizons.config.server.generation:
How many LOD generation requests per second should a client send? 
Also limits th' number o' client requests allowed ter stay in th' server's queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxGenerat: Sets th' distance allowed ter generate around th' player.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableReal: If true, clients will receive real-time LOD updates fer chunks outside th' client's render distance.
distanthorizons.config.server.realTimeUp: Sets th' distance th' player will receive updates around.
distanthorizons.config.server.synchroniz: If true, clients will receive updated LODs when joinin' or loadin' new LODs.
distanthorizons.config.server.syncOnLoad: Rate Limit fer Sync on Load

How many LOD sync requests per second should a client send? 
Also limits th' number o' client's requests allowed ter stay in th' server's queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxSyncOnL: Max Sync on Load Request Distance

Sets th' distance allowed ter be synchronized around th' player. 
Should be th' same or larger than maxGenerationRequestDistance in most cases.
distanthorizons.config.server.playerBand:
Maximum per-player speed fer uploadin' LODs ter th' clients, in KB/s. 
A value o' 0 disables th' limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.globalBand:
Maximum global speed fer uploadin' LODs ter th' clients, in KB/s. 
A value o' 0 disables th' limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableAdap:
Enables adaptive transfer speed based on client performance. 
If true, DH will adjust th' transfer rate on its own ter minimize connection lag. 
If false, transfer speed will stay fixed.
